![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/936cea1e20ef7bbc1eb66acf9dd564c61476f5bb68ee05e553b00aaf3f970dc3.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible? 

I. $x\in [-4,0]$

II. $x\in (-4,-2]$

III. $x\in (-3,1)$
questions.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.  

- The given function is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in [-4,0]$ and $x\in (-4,-2].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/a4499c2d4995c09b9ab6f8852cc2982f415f1650d65429c86df83800344106f4.png)

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $x\in (-3,1]$  because some lines will intersect the curve at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/cb0a462b3af10d15bb586f127baac45a74eecd5dc19848bda23664e75de968a4.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)={x}^{2}+2,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

I. $x\in (-2,2)$

II. $x\in [0,\infty )$

III. $x\in (-\infty ,0]$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)={x}^{2}+2$ can be obtained in the following way:

1\. Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

2\. Translate it by $2$ units up to get $f(x)={x}^{2}+2.$

  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/ff3d1ac7500d83574b8671b23e99d4a0f1dbd6ab9cebc906aa06ff2c21f95345.png)

  A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

3\. The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-2,2).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/a71ce036adc5dc0b15fce9e367a0c8512699dc6a7814f4e9a1886696d2abad6e.png)

4\. The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the intervals $x\in [0,\infty )$ and  $x\in (-\infty ,0].$ On these intervals, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/6858bd1fab8d9659c84fa941cd63ee9f509c8364dce0e753706c640ecfe6e9ec.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".
